source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 1 (ISLB A1) · lesson 7. Exercises reused from the lesson.
topic: Angels: made of light, always obeying Allah, and our two recording angels

learn.en: One angel is called a malak. Many angels are called malā'ikah.
learn.title: Malak and malā'ikah

learn.en: We are made from earth, but angels are made of pure light, so we cannot see them.
learn.title: Made of light

learn.en: Angels always obey Allah. They cannot choose to do wrong, and they never get tired of worshipping Him.
learn.title: Always obeying

learn.en: Some angels' names: Jibreel, Mika'eel, Israfeel and Ridwan. Jibreel brought the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
learn.title: Their names

learn.en: You have two angels with you all the time, writing down your good and bad actions — like helpers with a golden pen.
learn.title: Your two angels

learn.en: Angels take turns visiting us night and day, and they meet at the Fajr and Asr prayers.
learn.title: At Fajr and Asr

quiz.en: What did Allah create the angels from?
Which angel brought the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
What is the Arabic word for one angel?
True or false? We can easily see the angels walking around with our own eyes.
True or false? Every one of us has two special angels who stay with us all the time.
True or false? Sometimes angels make mistakes and choose to do the wrong thing.

think.q: Your classmate dropped their crayons and you helped pick them up, but the teacher didn't see. Who saw it?
think.a: Your recording angel wrote down your good deed — and Allah saw it too!

parents.summary: Angels (malāʾika) are made of light, always obey Allah, and two angels record our good and bad deeds.
parents.tip: Draw together: Haitham doing a kind deed, with a golden pen beside him.
